data.gender_notes: Ozian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew language, Ozian is a name of Hebrew origin which means 'God is my helper'. This name is associated with the Bible character Ozias, a king of Judah in the Old Testament. As a Christian name, Ozian is a symbol of faith and trust in God's assistance. The name Ozian carries the meaning “God is my helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ozian usually hope their child will grow to embody god is my helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ozian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is my helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ozian total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ozian is rooted in the Old Testament where we find the biblical character Ozias, a king of Judah who ruled in the late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE. King Ozias was a faithful servant of the Lord and an exemplary ruler who led his people in righteousness and justice. The name Ozian as a Christian name reflects the cultural values of faith, obedience, and trust in God's guidance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ozian holds deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of God's presence and assistance in our lives. It is a promise that no matter what challenges we may face, God is there to help us and support us through the journey of life. For Christians, the name Ozian embodies the belief that God is our ultimate source of strength, reassurance, and hope. The name encourages us to trust in God's plan for our lives and to seek His guidance in every decision we make. Overall, the name Ozian is a powerful reminder of the Christian faith's central tenet that God is with us always, and that He will never abandon us.

He is said to have lived in solitude in a cave near the town of Gerano, in Italy. His writings, which include letters and treatises, have been influential in Christian mysticism and asceticism.

historical_references.reference: Ozian is also associated with the legend of the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus. According to the story, seven young men who were Christians were put to sleep by God to protect them from persecution during the reign of Emperor Decius in the 3rd century AD. They were said to have awakened during the reign of Emperor Theodosius I in the late 4th century AD, and Ozian was one of those who greeted them upon their awakening.
